benefits.name: Disabled Veteran Property Tax Relief
benefits.description: Tennessee provides property tax relief on a primary residence for veterans who qualify under one of several categories: certain enumerated service-connected disabilities (paraplegia, permanent paralysis of both legs from a spinal cord or brain injury, loss or loss of use of two or more limbs, or legal blindness), a service-connected permanent and total disability as determined by the VA, or 100% disability resulting from former prisoner-of-war status. Relief is calculated against a maximum market value of $175,000 — the exact dollar rebate/exemption depends on the local county tax rate, which was not itemized on the official page. The Tennessee Department of Veterans Services page also references 'Public Chapter No. 1065' as documenting recent program changes, but the specific substance of that amendment was not detailed on the page read this session, so no change details beyond the $175,000 cap are claimed here.
benefits.value: Property tax relief on a primary residence, calculated against a maximum market value of $175,000

otherReqs: Applicant must own and occupy the property as primary residence

Qualifies via VA-determined service-connected permanent and total disability, specific enumerated catastrophic disabilities (paraplegia, loss of two or more limbs, legal blindness), or 100% disability from POW status
Apply through the County Trustee's office (or city collecting official for property inside city limits)

application.agency: Tennessee Department of Veterans Services / County Trustee's Office
documentation: VA disability rating letter confirming qualifying service-connected disability
Proof of ownership and occupancy of primary residence

benefits.name: Tennessee State Veterans Homes
benefits.description: Tennessee operates five state veterans homes providing skilled nursing and short-term rehabilitative / long-term care, located in Humboldt (W.D. 'Bill' Manning TSVH), Murfreesboro, Clarksville (Brigadier General Wendell H. Gilbert TSVH), Knoxville (Ben Atchley TSVH), and Cleveland. They are operated by the Tennessee State Veterans Home Board in coordination with the Tennessee Department of Veterans Services. The tn.gov overview page confirms locations, contact numbers, and the operating board, but does not itself publish detailed medical-admission eligibility criteria, per-diem costs, or residency requirements — those live on the separate tsvh.org site, which was not fetched this session, so specific admission requirements beyond 'honorably discharged veterans, spouses, widows/widowers, and Gold Star parents' (per search results, not independently confirmed via fetch) are not asserted here as verified fact.
benefits.value: Skilled nursing and short-term rehabilitative / long-term care

otherReqs: Honorable discharge (per secondary sources; not independently confirmed on the fetched tn.gov page)
Detailed medical admission criteria are set by the Tennessee State Veterans Home Board and were not confirmed this session

application.agency: Tennessee State Veterans Home Board / Tennessee Department of Veterans Services
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of military service

benefits.name: In-State Tuition for Veterans Using VA Education Benefits
benefits.description: Veterans (or dependents) using U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs education benefits such as the Post-9/11 GI Bill or the Fry Scholarship, who are enrolled at a Tennessee public institution of higher education and living in Tennessee while using those benefits, are exempt from out-of-state tuition and fees regardless of their formal state of residency. This implements the federal Choice Act requirement. Service members who want to transfer Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits to a dependent must complete the transfer while still on active duty.
benefits.value: Exemption from out-of-state tuition and fees at Tennessee public colleges/universities for qualifying VA-education-benefit users

otherReqs: Must be using VA education benefits (e.g., Post-9/11 GI Bill or Fry Scholarship) at the enrolling institution
Must be living in Tennessee while enrolled and using the benefit, regardless of formal state of residency
Post-9/11 GI Bill benefit transfers to dependents must be completed while the service member is still on active duty

documentation: VA Certificate of Eligibility for education benefits
Proof of Tennessee residency/domicile while enrolled

benefits.name: Tuition Waiver for Dependents of Veterans Killed, POW, or MIA
benefits.description: A dependent child (under 23, though the age limit is not strictly applied per the statute referenced) or spouse of a veteran who was killed or died as a direct result of injuries received during a qualifying period of armed conflict, or who was officially reported as a prisoner-of-war or missing-in-action, is entitled to free tuition, maintenance fees, student activity fees, and registration fees at Tennessee public colleges and universities. The veteran-parent must have been a Tennessee resident at the time of death, and the dependent cannot concurrently receive similar benefits under Public Law 634 or comparable federal programs. This page describes only the killed/died/POW/MIA program; separate proposed state legislation (e.g., HB1604/SB1576) that would extend a comparable waiver to dependents of veterans with a 100% permanent-and-total service-connected disability was found via search but could not be confirmed as enacted law against an official source this session, so it is not included as a verified benefit here.
benefits.value: Free tuition, maintenance fees, student activity fees, and registration fees at Tennessee public colleges/universities

otherReqs: Dependent child must be under 23 (age limitation not strictly applied per the statute)
Veteran-parent must have been a Tennessee resident at time of death
Cannot be receiving benefits under Public Law 634 or other similar federal laws
Must present a certificate from the U.S. Government establishing eligibility

documentation: Certificate from the U.S. Government establishing qualifying status (killed in action, died of service-related injury, POW, or MIA)

benefits.name: State Employment Veterans' Preference (TEAM Act)
benefits.description: Veterans who meet the minimum qualifications for open state 'preferred service' positions are guaranteed an interview. Where a veteran and another applicant have equal qualifications, skills, abilities, competencies, and knowledge, hiring preference goes to the veteran; a supervisor who bypasses an eligible veteran for a non-veteran must document the reason in writing. During reductions in force, veterans receive 60 months of credit toward time-of-service calculations. The preference also extends to eligible surviving spouses of veterans who had a 100% service-connected disability or who died in the line of duty, provided the spouse is a qualified Tennessee voter or 2+-year state resident and has not remarried. Documentation of military service, honorable discharge, disability, death, or residence must be provided to the Department of Human Resources.
benefits.value: Guaranteed interview for qualified veterans; tie-break hiring preference when qualifications are equal; 60-month RIF service credit

otherReqs: Documentation of military service, honorable discharge, disability, death, or residence required by the Dept. of Human Resources

Surviving-spouse preference limited to spouses of veterans who were 100% service-connected disabled or died in the line of duty, who are a qualified TN voter or 2+ year TN resident, and who have not remarried

application.agency: Tennessee Department of Human Resources / Tennessee Department of Veterans Services
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge
VA disability rating letter (for surviving-spouse preference based on 100% disability)

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate (Fee-Waived)
benefits.description: Veterans with a permanent and total (100%) VA disability rating incurred in or aggravated by active military service can obtain a Disabled Veteran license plate. A letter from the federal Department of Veterans Affairs verifying the permanent and total rating with an effective date is required. The first plate is issued at no cost; a second plate carries a $26.50 annual renewal fee ($28.15 initial), and subsequent plates carry a $26.50 annual renewal fee ($29.80 initial) — except plates issued before May 19, 2014, which were grandfathered to allow up to two free plates. The specific VR-13 Department of Revenue support article describing this plate could not be fetched this session (the page returned an HTTP 403), so form-number details from that page are not included here; the eligibility and fee figures above come from the tn.gov Department of Revenue plate page that was successfully fetched.
benefits.value: First plate free; additional plates $26.50/year renewal ($28.15-$29.80 initial fee)

otherReqs: Vehicle registered in Tennessee
Passenger vehicles and motorcycles eligible
Plates issued before May 19, 2014 were grandfathered to allow up to two free plates

application.agency: Tennessee Department of Revenue, Vehicle Services
documentation: Letter from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs verifying permanent and total disability with an effective date

benefits.name: Motor Vehicle Privilege Tax Exemption for 100% Disabled Veterans
benefits.description: Any Tennessee veteran with a 100 percent permanent, total, service-connected disability as determined by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, or any former prisoner-of-war, is exempt from the county motor vehicle privilege tax upon submitting evidence of the disability to the county officer responsible for collecting that tax.
benefits.value: Exemption from the county motor vehicle privilege tax

otherReqs: Evidence of qualifying disability (or POW status) must be submitted to the county officer who collects the tax

application.agency: County Clerk / Tennessee Department of Veterans Services
documentation: VA disability rating letter confirming 100% permanent and total disability, or documentation of former POW status

benefits.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing License
benefits.description: Tennessee residents who are 100% permanently and totally service-connected disabled may obtain a permanent combination sport hunting and fishing license for a one-time $10 fee. Separately, Tennessee residents who are 30% or more disabled 'by reason of service in any war' may obtain sport fishing and hunting licenses without paying any fee. TWRA accepts a VA certification as evidence of the service-connected disability. Some secondary sources (not the official tn.gov page fetched this session) claim the 100%-tier license never expires; that specific claim was not stated on the official page read this session, so it is noted as unconfirmed rather than asserted as fact. Quota hunts, WMA permits, and certain other permits still require separate fees regardless of this license.
benefits.value: One-time $10 fee for a permanent combination hunting/fishing license (100% P&T tier); no-fee license for war-era veterans 30%+ disabled

otherReqs: 100% permanent-and-total service-connected disabled veterans: one-time $10 fee for a permanent license
Veterans 30% or more disabled 'by reason of service in any war': license issued without any fee
TWRA accepts a VA certification as proof of service-connected disability
Quota hunts, WMA permits, and county doe permits still require separate fees
